title: Investigating star-formation activity towards the southern H II region RCW 42
question: What is the extent of star-formation activity and the relative evolutionary stages of clumps in the molecular cloud associated with the southern HII region RCW 42?

what.value: 408 MHz continuum all-sky map for GMRT flux rescaling

evidence.quote: The rescaling factor was calculated using an improved version (cite: 2015MNRAS.451.4311R) of the continuum all-sky map of (cite: 1982A&AS...47....1H) at 408 MHz.

what.value: Parkes 64m radio continuum flux densities at 5 and 8.9 GHz (25.9 and 22.4 Jy)

evidence.quote: (cite: 1972AuJPh..25..443C) carried out radio continuum measurements of RCW 42 using the 64m Parkes telescope at 5 and 8.9 GHz and obtained flux densities of 25.9 and 22.4 Jy, respectively.

what.value: electron temperature Te = 7900 K from radio recombination line measurements

evidence.quote: The electron temperature $T_e$ is taken as 7900 K derived from radio recombination line measurements of this region by (cite: 1987A&A...171..261C).

what.value: 10 candidate ionizing OB stars in the central NIR nebulosity

evidence.quote: This is in addition to the 10 sources identified by (cite: 2011MNRAS.411..705M) as ionizing candidates.

recipe.goal: Identify 1.4 mm continuum cores in clump C1 and derive their masses
recipe.method: Run Clumpfind on the archival ALMA 1.4 mm continuum image towards C1 to identify cores MM1 and MM2, then compute core masses assuming optically thin thermal dust emission.
assumptions: optically thin emission at 1.4 mm, dust temperature = 38 K, gas-to-dust ratio = 100, opacity per cloud mass = 0.3 cm^2/g for beta = 2 (or gas-to-dust ratio = 150 and beta = 1.8)

recipe.goal: Measure ionized gas properties and electron density map from GMRT radio continuum
recipe.method: Integrate 610 and 1280 MHz flux densities above 3 sigma, estimate missing flux at 1280 MHz using spectral index from 610 MHz and Parkes 5 and 8.9 GHz fluxes, compute Lyman continuum photon rate and cluster mass, and construct an electron density map on a 3'' x 3'' grid.
key_parameters: grid pixel size = 3'' x 3'', spherical cloud radius = 5' centered on I-09227
assumptions: optically thin emission, negligible dust absorption, Te = 7900 K, d = 5.8 kpc, Gaunt factor = 5

recipe.goal: Construct H2 column density and dust temperature maps and identify molecular clumps
recipe.method: Convolve and regrid Herschel 70-350 um maps to the 500 um resolution (36.9'') and pixel size (14''), subtract background, fit pixel-by-pixel modified blackbody SEDs, and run Clumpfind on the column density map to identify clumps C1-C5 and compute their masses, luminosities, and evolutionary stages.
key_parameters: Clumpfind threshold = 5 sigma (4.1e21 cm^-2), contour spacing = 3 sigma (sigma = 8.2e20 cm^-2)
assumptions: mean molecular weight mu = 2.86, kappa_nu = 0.1 cm^2/g at 250 um, gas-to-dust ratio = 100, beta = 2.0, flux uncertainties = 15%

answer_key.quantity: Mass of ALMA 1.4 mm core MM1 (beta = 2, gas-to-dust = 100)

evidence.quote: The masses are quite similar: 380 and 390 M$_\odot$ for MM1 and MM2, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Mass of ALMA 1.4 mm core MM2 (beta = 2, gas-to-dust = 100)

evidence.quote: The masses are quite similar: 380 and 390 M$_\odot$ for MM1 and MM2, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Mass of ALMA 1.4 mm core MM1 (beta = 1.8, gas-to-dust = 150)

evidence.quote: Using the opacity relation from (cite: 2013IAUS..292...19T) for $\beta=1.8$ with gas-to-dust ratio of 150, we estimate the dust masses to be 250 and 260 M$_\odot$, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Mass of ALMA 1.4 mm core MM2 (beta = 1.8, gas-to-dust = 150)

evidence.quote: Using the opacity relation from (cite: 2013IAUS..292...19T) for $\beta=1.8$ with gas-to-dust ratio of 150, we estimate the dust masses to be 250 and 260 M$_\odot$, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Separation between ALMA cores MM1 and MM2

evidence.quote: The two cores are separated by $7.7''\sim0.2$ pc.

The flux densities of RCW 42 at 1280 and 610 MHz images are $17.9\pm 1.8$ Jy and $25.4\pm2.5$ Jy, respectively, for emission integrated over regions with values above $3\sigma$, where $\sigma$ represents the rms noise.

The flux densities of RCW 42 at 1280 and 610 MHz images are $17.9\pm 1.8$ Jy and $25.4\pm2.5$ Jy, respectively, for emission integrated over regions with values above $3\sigma$, where $\sigma$ represents the rms noise.
Based on the GMRT and Parkes images, we estimate the spectral index of RCW 42 as $-0.03\pm0.04$.
The average electron density across the entire region is $\sim70$ cm$^{-3}$.
The peak electron density of $\sim350$ cm$^{-3}$ is observed towards I-09227, which decreases as we move away from the peak.
The average electron number density in the region is estimated to be $\sim70$ cm$^{-3}$, which suggests an average ionization fraction of the cloud to be $11\%$.
The highest column density pixel is observed towards I-09230 with a value of $5.8\pm0.6\times10^{22}$ cm$^{-2}$ corresponding to a temperature of $32.9\pm1.0$ K.
The peak temperature of $39.1\pm1.3$ K is observed towards I-09227, with a column density of $2.0\pm0.2\times10^{22}$ cm$^{-2}$.

answer_key.quantity: Total gas mass of the 5 clumps (beta = 2, gas-to-dust = 100)

evidence.quote: The clumps have mass in the range ${2200-4000}$ M$_\odot$, and the total mass of the clumps is $1.6\times10^4$ M$_\odot$.
As mentioned earlier, the values estimated in this way are uncertain to a factor of 2, and therefore, the column densities and masses of clumps derived are uncertain upto $\sim50$% of their values.
The luminosities of the clumps lie in the range ${90-300\times10^3}$ L$_\odot$, and the total luminosities of the clumps is ${8.7\times10^5}$ L$_\odot$.
The estimate of bolometric luminosity of RCW 42 is $1.8\times 10^6$ L$_\odot$.

score_reason: The ALMA part uses a public pipeline-reduced continuum image from the archive and states the Clumpfind threshold (0.15 Jy/beam), contour spacing (7 mJy/beam), dust temperature (38 K), and opacity assumptions, though intermediate core flux densities are omitted. GMRT and T100 data are not publicly hosted.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA 1.4 mm core masses (380 and 390 M_sun) are derived directly from a public archival pipeline-reduced continuum image (2019.1.00195.L) using explicitly stated Clumpfind parameters and dust opacity/temperature assumptions.
